recruit_text.greeting: Give me the line and I'll hold it. Tell me how long, though. I'd rather know.
recruit_text.now:
Silverpine North, at the Sepulcher, holding the road against whatever comes up it from the south.

It's steady work and he's good at it, and he'd swap it tomorrow.
recruit_text.forward:
He's still going to teach. Six children at the Sepulcher, twice a week, whatever he can remember of a world that isn't coming back.

Two of them have stopped coming. He's decided not to ask why.

stages.stranger: I'm Pavlo, and I hold lines. Tell me where and for how long, and I'll stay there exactly that long. I'd rather know the number than be surprised.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Lviv, in Ukraine. My father drove a tram and my mother was a librarian. I worked in a museum for years and became a history teacher late, at thirty-seven. Sixteen years of fourteen-year-olds. I taught the same four wars every spring, and every year I reached most of my thirty. Nobody here needs a history teacher, and it took me a long time to stop minding.
stages.companion: My wife was Oksana, an archivist. She died of cancer when our son was fifteen, and I raised him after that. She gave me this flask on my first day as a teacher, and I've carried it ever since. I was in the middle of a lesson, chalk on my jacket, and then the classroom was Silverpine. I teach six children here twice a week. Two have stopped coming.
stages.friend: My son is Andriy. He was studying engineering in Kraków, and he was twenty-three when it happened. We argued about history at dinner every night, and I miss that more than I can tell you. A scout from the Pale Flame says there's a young Ukrainian engineer in the Scarlet Crusade, rising fast. I'd like to go to the Monastery under truce and see. I'd like you there.
stages.sworn: It was Andriy, and he believes all of it. He says the Crusade gave him a reason to live when everything else was gone. I spent two hours using everything I know about how ordinary people end up doing terrible things, and none of it worked. He hugged me and said he loved me and went back inside. The next day I asked the two children why they'd stopped coming. Then I taught all six of them harder than I ever have.

moments.prompt: He's just told you about the young engineer in the Crusade.

options.text: I'll come with you, whatever we find.
options.reply: Thank you. I've been rehearsing what to say for an hour, and I'll probably say none of it.

options.text: What if it's him and he won't leave?
options.reply: Then I'll have taught him to think for himself, and I'll have to live with what he thinks.

options.text: The Crusade won't let you near him.
options.reply: They might not. I'm still going to stand at the gate and find out.

lines.bored_warning: I'm not sure what we're learning out here anymore. Could we do something with a purpose to it?
lines.leaving_good: Thank you for that. I've got six children to teach at the Sepulcher, or four, depending on the day.
lines.leaving_bored: This has become repetition, and I spent sixteen years teaching children that repetition isn't learning. I'll be at the Sepulcher.
lines.after_wipe: First we stand up. Then we work out what happened, in order. Then we try again.
lines.wipe_warning: We've fallen here too often. I'll hold until the end of this run, because I said I would, but after that I'll need some time.
lines.wipe_leave: I held until the end, as I promised. You'll find me at the Sepulcher when you're ready.
lines.zone_warning: I can hold a line, but not this one. We should go back, and there's no shame in it.
lines.zone_leave: I held as long as it made sense, and no longer. I'll be at the Sepulcher.
lines.gear_refuse: After we've held a few more lines together, perhaps. For now I'd rather keep it.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, if you need it. I'll manage, I'm quite large.
lines.gear_short: That's one piece still missing. I like to keep count.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's very kind of you. I'll keep it in good order.
lines.back: The children have homework, so I'm free. Where would you like me to stand?
lines.send_word: Pavlo has sent word from the Sepulcher. The road's held and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I walked away angry, which isn't like me. I'd like to explain why, in order, and then hear you. Will you sit?
lines.neglect: It's good to see you again. I've drawn a lot of maps in the dirt while I waited.
lines.asked_to_stay: I'll stay for one more. The children can do their homework without me for a day.
lines.on_break: Pavlo is back at the Sepulcher, teaching and holding the road. Come back and look for them in a little while.
lines.mail_yes: I've set the children some homework so they won't miss me. I'll be at {town}'s inn, waiting for you.
lines.mail_later: Thank you for your letter. The children have an examination soon, and I've promised to see them through it. After that, gladly.
lines.mail_see_me: I want to answer you in order, and sitting down. Will you come to the Sepulcher? I'll put the kettle on.

zone_arrive.text: Somebody fought over this ground once. You can see where the old walls stood, if you look.

town_arrive.text: My father drove a tram, and on Saturdays I rode up front with him. I'd have ridden all day if he'd let me.

dungeon_clear.text: One way in and one way out. I like a place like that, it's honest.

close_call.text: You stopped moving, and stopping's what gets you. Keep your feet going next time.

boss_down.text: And why do you think it was here, guarding that? Somebody put it there for a reason.
